problem: It was unknown why ostensibly 'map-free' neural navigation agents (CNN+RNN, transformers) achieve near-perfect PointGoal navigation; whether they build implicit maps had not been shown, and animal-navigation studies cannot isolate mapping from landmarks, olfaction and other cues.
motivation: Understanding the mechanism behind map-free agents matters scientifically and for safety when deploying them. By using 'blind' agents that sense only egomotion, with generic LSTMs and no mapping bias, alternative mechanisms can be ruled out, so any map-like structure in memory must emerge from goal-driven RL alone.
key_idea: Train blind (egomotion-only) LSTM agents for PointGoal navigation with RL and show through probing that their hidden memory contains implicit, task-dependent metric maps that support shortcuts, collision detection, and occupancy decoding.
insight: Memory is essential: memoryless agents get ~0% success and performance does not saturate until ~1000 steps of memory. A probe initialized with the trained agent's final memory takes shortcuts (SPL 85.0 vs 62.9 for the agent), whereas memory from a random-weight LSTM gives no gain over zero memory. That comparison shows the map is a learned behavior. Excursions are harder to decode from memory than non-excursion path segments, so the maps are selective and task-dependent. Map-building may need a challenging, 'no trivial solution' setting, since decoding maps from Depth-equipped agents gave mixed results.
method: Blind PointGoal agent: 3-layer LSTM (512-d) fed goal vector, GPS, compass, previous action and a near-goal indicator; trained with DD-PPO for ~2B steps on Gibson (411 scenes) and MP3D (72 scenes) with episodic coordinates and a shaped reward.

Collision-neuron analysis: a linear (L1-sparse) classifier on the frozen (h,c) predicts whether the last action collided (98% accuracy; 10 of 3072 neurons give 96%); t-SNE shows 4 clusters of previous action and collision outcome.
Memory-length ablation: at test time the LSTM is unrolled from zero state over only the last k observations, giving performance vs. memory budget k; also agents trained at fixed budgets up to k=256.

Probe / memory transplant (SecondNav): a second blind agent, initialized with the first agent's final (h,c), navigates S→T or T→S. It is compared against AllZeroMemory and UntrainedAgentMemory controls, and quantified with Chamfer-based Excursion Removal and Free Space Inference.

Occupancy-map decoder: a CoordConv/CoordUpConv network decodes a 96×96 top-down navigable/non-navigable grid from the final (h,c), restricted to within 2.5 m of visited locations, and is compared against untrained-LSTM memory by IoU.
Past/future position decoding: an MLP predicts the agent's location k steps in the past or future from (h,c); errors on manually labeled excursions show that excursions are forgotten.
Baselines/controls: clairvoyant Bug algorithm with an oracle for wall-following direction; single-environment agent with global coordinates (memorizes shortest paths, 100% train / 0% test).

setting.backbone: 3-layer LSTM (512-d hidden), trained from scratch with DD-PPO; separate small MLP/CNN probes and decoders
setting.model_size: 3-layer LSTM with 512-d hidden state; parameter count not stated
setting.training_data: RL in Habitat on Gibson (411 scenes) and Matterport3D (72 scenes), ~2 billion steps; no extra or synthetic data; decoders and probes trained on trajectories from the trained agent on training scenes
setting.observation: egomotion only (idealized GPS+Compass, no vision or other sensing) plus the goal vector and previous action
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT 10°, TURN RIGHT 10°, STOP; max 2000 steps
setting.privileged: none for the agent; the clairvoyant Bug baseline uses an oracle for the wall-following direction; probes use the agent's final memory by design

numbers.extra: 18 MP3D test scenes, 1008 episodes (Habitat PointNav episodes), 2000-step limit, success radius 0.2 m, noiseless actuation and sensing

numbers.backbone: 3-layer LSTM probe initialized with blind agent's final memory
numbers.extra: Second navigation using the first agent's final memory; episodes where the agent failed (~5%) removed; 5 agent-probe pairs

numbers.backbone: 3-layer LSTM probe initialized with blind agent's final memory
numbers.extra: Reverse navigation using the agent's final memory; failed agent episodes removed

numbers_note: Occupancy-map IoU (32.5% vs 12.5% for trained vs untrained memory), collision-classifier accuracy (98%) and memory-length curves are also reported, but they are not navigation benchmark numbers. Memory-length results are given only in figures. The paper text prints 32.5/12.5 while the Fig. 4 labels say 32.4/12.4.
results: Blind agents reach 95.1% success and 62.9 SPL in unseen MP3D scenes, similar in success to a Depth-camera agent (94.0) and higher in SPL than the clairvoyant Bug algorithm (46.0). Transplanting the trained memory into a probe raises SPL to 85.0 vs 71.1 (zero memory) and 72.0 (random-LSTM memory). Occupancy maps decode with 32.5% IoU vs 12.5% for untrained memory.
limitations: Only ground-based agents in digitized houses with strong layout priors, with noiseless actuation and sensing; generalization to other settings such as drones in forests is unclear.
Evidence for maps in sighted (Depth) agents is inconclusive, so the explanation of map-free sighted agents is only partial.
Memory is reset every episode, the map is an implicit LSTM representation, and no mechanistic account is given of how it is built or what else is stored.
builds_on: Habitat PointGoalNav map-free agents (Wijmans et al. 2020)
